summary: Federal Reserve Board unanimously voted to raise interest rate paid on reserve balances to 1.65% and increased the primary credit rate by 0.75 percentage points to 1.75%, both effective June 16, 2022. FOMC directed the Desk to maintain federal funds rate in target range of 1.50% to 1.75%, with overnight repo minimum bid rate at 1.75% and reverse repo offering rate at 1.55%.
why_it_matters: This implementation note details the operational mechanics of the June 2022 FOMC decision, which raised rates by 75 basis points—the largest single meeting increase since 1994—as the Fed aggressively fought inflation.
macro_context: June 2022 FOMC meeting; Fed was in aggressive tightening mode following CPI readings exceeding 8%. The 75bps hike was larger than the 50bps most economists expected, signaling Fed's willingness to move forcefully against inflation.
market_structure_context: Repo operations maintained with $500B aggregate limit for overnight repos and $160B per-counterparty limit for reverse repos. Treasury rollovers capped at $30B/month, MBS reinvestments capped at $17.5B/month.
